DISABLED IN CI 2026-11-20: CI run 44683774390 (browser group, commit 8d44702) rendered https://www.emploi.ma/recherche-jobs-maroc in headless UC Chrome and the runner's datacenter IP was served the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge; the listing never exposed its ad links within the 60 s wait and discover_detail_paths aborted with BrowserChallengeError (0 records). The same config clears the challenge from a residential IP in ~8 s and parsed 20/20 ads locally, so the block is IP reputation, not the config; no config knob changes the source IP. Kept in the browser group with its site config so it runs locally and can be re-enabled when the block lifts. Framework change measured here: error_markers makes an origin 502/503/504 page a per-ad fetch failure instead of storing a 60-word 'Gateway time-out' as the job description.

empleate.gob.es (Empléate, Spain) - SEPE's own public employment portal. No key, no registration, no proxy. robots.txt (/empleate/robots.txt) is 'User-agent: *' / 'Allow: /' with no Crawl-delay; only the logged-in employer/candidate areas are disallowed and this scraper touches none of them. Discovery and content are the SAME request: the SPA's public Solr endpoint GET /empleate/open/offersearch/selectBuscador?q.op=AND&q=*&wt=json&fq=checkVisible:true&rows=100&start=N&sort=fechaCreacion desc,id desc returns the whole posting inside the listing document (titulo, creador, contenido description, ciudadF/provinciaF/paisF, fechaCreacion, salarioMin/Max, tipoContratoN, jornada, modality, horario, experienciaF), so a run costs one request per 100 ads and needs no per-ad detail call (the SPA's open/offer/load/<id> adds only display formatting). Measured 2026-11-20: numFound=26073 visible ads; rows is silently capped at 100 server-side (rows=200 returns 100); start pages to the very end (start=26072 returned the last document); the default order is relevance so sort is mandatory, and fechaCreacion desc alone is not deterministic because dozens of ads share one second in the nightly SNE batch - the 'id desc' tie-breaker was measured to give stable, non-overlapping page boundaries. Freshness: 760 new ads/24h and 3,636/7d; the newest ~12,000 documents are one nightly SNE batch that carries no creador/experienciaF/horario (measured at start=12000: 43% creador, 23% experienciaF, 37% horario), so max_env defaults to 1000 with fresh_rows=800 (above the measured daily volume, so the batch is covered) and the archive tail rotates one window-width per hour across the four scheduled runs; start_offset, when pinned, is an ABSOLUTE corpus offset (page-aligned and pushed past the fresh region) so a manual or test run is reproducible. Employment mapping uses the portal's own open/master/contracttypes (0 unspecified, 1 ContractToHire, 2 Contract, 3 Temporary, 4 SelfEmployed, 5 Internship, 6 Apprenticeship) combined with jornada from open/master/daytypes (1 COMPLETA, 2 PARCIAL, 3 INDIFERENTE, 4 FLEXIBLE), and modality (facet: 0 No informado 24091, 1 Presencial 1885, 2/3 remote, 4 Mixto 83) treats 0 as on-site. Salary: salarioMin/Max are Spanish-formatted strings ('21,000', '16261,86'); '0' - and verSalarioMin/Max='0' - means missing, not zero; the offer page renders 'Brutos/ano' while the SPA-generated JSON-LD says unitText MONTH, so amounts are stored as yearly EUR following the visible label and the inconsistency plus the raw strings are recorded in raw_payload. Location: '<ciudadF>; <provinciaF>; <ISO2>' - 2,478 distinct municipalities, of which only Madrid and Barcelona collide with a seeded city and both are Spanish; paisF maps ESPANA->ES plus 11 foreign labels (HOLANDA->NL, FRANCIA->FR, ANDORRA->AD, ...). Scope added for this source: an Andorra ref.countries row, 52 Spanish provinces as ref.regions (the portal's exact provinciaF facet values, seeded byte-identically because the resolver matches region_name exactly), and SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['empleate_es']=ES. TLS: the host sends ONLY its leaf (O=Servicio Publico de Empleo Estatal, CN=*.empleate.gob.es), issued by 'Entrust OV TLS Issuing RSA CA 2' under the Sectigo Public Server Authentication Root R46 that certifi already ships; with the intermediate omitted, requests/curl_cffi/openssl all fail 'unable to get local issuer certificate' (Windows Schannel succeeds only because the OS had cached the intermediate). The missing intermediate - fetched from the leaf's own AIA URL - is shipped in the package (src/job_market_intel/scrapers/empleate_es/certs/) and appended to a copy of certifi's roots, verified with openssl verify -> OK; certificate verification therefore stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

chiletrabajos.cl (Chiletrabajos, Chile) - a large generalist Chilean board. No key, no registration, no proxy, and no browser. Discovery is the ADVERTISED sitemap (https://www.chiletrabajos.cl/sitemap.xml): measured 2026-10-09 it is a single <urlset> of 32,993 /trabajo/<slug>-<id> URLs in newest-first order (top lastmod 2026-10-09T03:29:15Z, bottom 2026-07-26), ~9.0 MB. Each ad is one request: every /trabajo/ page carries a Schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block (alongside a BreadcrumbList and a related-ads ItemList) with title, hiringOrganization.name/logo, datePosted ('YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'), validThrough (ISO), employmentType, industry, jobLocation.address (addressLocality=comuna, addressRegion=ISO 3166-2:CL 2-letter code, addressCountry=CL, postalCode) and a plain-text description; baseSalary is a MonetaryAmount whose value.Value (note the capital V) is a string or integer, and 0 means undisclosed (stored as no salary, not zero pesos). The region code is mapped onto the 16 full region names seeded in ref.regions (region_code CL-XX) and the ad's own comuna onto ref.cities, so a posting resolves at city level where seeded and region level otherwise. Capped runs always take the newest 120 rows (fresh_rows) plus a rotating slice of the tail whose start advances one budget-width per calendar day, so older ads are covered over successive runs instead of the same first page being re-read forever. robots.txt: the default 'User-agent: *' group disallows only /partners/ and /ofertasmuchomas (neither touched) and advertises this sitemap; a separate 'User-agent: Scrapy,proximic / Disallow: /' block is a targeted bot ban and neither token is sent; no Crawl-delay is set, so a polite 1 s gap between requests is kept. NOTE on reachability: the site resolves worldwide (US/Canada/Brazil/Germany probes get HTTP 200) but was unreachable from the Bangladesh build network (TCP 80/443 timeout), so the parser was built from archived markup and verified end-to-end in CI (GitHub Actions, United States). Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

maukerja.my (MauKerja, Malaysia) - AJobThing's large generalist Malaysian board. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. Discovery is the ADVERTISED sitemap chain: /sitemap.xml (sitemapindex, 17 children) -> /mk_job.xml (index) -> /mk_job1.xml (<urlset>, 46,652 /job/<id>-<slug> ad URLs, ~9.0 MB, newest-first, measured 2026-11-20); the walk follows only children whose file name is a job sitemap (mk_job.xml, mk_job1.xml, ...) so it finds the job sitemap while mk_company_job*.xml and mk_jobsearch*.xml are skipped. The /jobsearch/all-jobs listing path is Cloudflare-protected (HTTP 403 'Just a moment...'), which is why discovery uses the published sitemaps. Each ad is one request: every /job/ page carries a Schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block (alongside a BreadcrumbList) with title, hiringOrganization.name/logo, identifier.value (the ad id), datePosted/validThrough (ISO-8601 Z), employmentType (a list of Schema.org codes), baseSalary (MonetaryAmount -> QuantitativeValue with value/minValue/maxValue and unitText MONTH; an all-zero value means unpublished, stored as no salary, not zero ringgit), salaryCurrency MYR, skills and jobBenefits (lists), occupationalCategory and a plain-text description. jobLocation.address is addressLocality/addressRegion/addressCountry; addressRegion is usually a state but is sometimes the federal-territory form WP Kuala Lumpur (normalised to Kuala Lumpur) or a bare postal code (rejected), and addressCountry is MY with the occasional SG. jobLocationType was absent on every ad sampled, so nothing is inferred remote from prose. Roughly one ad in twenty-five returns HTTP 200 with no JobPosting block (stable on retry); such an ad is skipped and counted as a failure rather than stored half-empty. Capped runs always take the newest 120 rows (fresh_rows) plus a rotating slice of the tail whose start advances one budget-width per calendar day, so older ads are covered over successive runs instead of the same first page being re-read forever. robots.txt (200, 1,214 bytes) bans AI crawler tokens (none sent) and disallows /jobs/, /job/read/, /job/*/search, /job/apply-job?*, /api/*, /search/*, /job-region/ and others - none of which this scraper touches - and advertises the sitemap; no Crawl-delay is set, so a polite 1 s gap is kept. The board is Malaysian and its few Singapore ads carry their own SG country segment, so the MY home-country fallback is correct. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

jobup.ch (JobCloud, Switzerland) - JobCloud AG's French-Swiss commercial board and a distinct inventory from its jobs_ch sibling. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. Discovery is the board's ADVERTISED sitemap index https://www.jobup.ch/sitemaps/jobup/en/sitemap.xml (sitemapindex, 20 children, measured 2026-11-20); the walk follows only children under the /job/ path, so .../job/sitemap.job-en.xml.gz (<urlset>, 30,590 /en/jobs/detail/<uuid>/ ad URLs, gzip 807 KB -> 5.9 MB inflated, written oldest-first) is found while the category, company, region and search sitemaps are skipped, and a future paginated sitemap.job-en_N.xml.gz is picked up automatically. The English and French job sitemaps hold the same UUIDs (30,590 vs 30,589 on 2026-11-20), so the English one is used and a job is not stored twice. Each ad is one request: every /en/jobs/detail/<uuid>/ page carries a Schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block (alongside a BreadcrumbList) with title, description (HTML), datePosted/validThrough (ISO-8601 with an offset), hiringOrganization.name/logo/sameAs, identifier (PropertyValue.value = the ad UUID), employmentType, baseSalary and jobLocation. employmentType is EITHER a list of Schema.org codes (['FULL_TIME']) OR a prose string ('Permanent position', 'Temporary', 'Apprenticeship'); a list holding two different codes is stored as no type rather than picking one, and 'Permanent position' has no matching reference code so it is also no type (the raw value stays in raw_payload). baseSalary is a MonetaryAmount (currency CHF) whose value is a QuantitativeValue with minValue/maxValue and unitText YEAR when a salary is published; roughly a third of the sampled ads carried a block and half of those had an EMPTY QuantitativeValue, which is stored as undisclosed (salary_disclosed=false), not zero francs. jobLocation.address is addressLocality/addressRegion/addressCountry; addressCountry was CH on 100% of a 60-ad sample; addressLocality is often absent and, when present, noisy ('Lachen SZ (8853 Lachen)', 'Haag (Rheintal) (9469 Buchs (SG))', 'Ilanz - Via Crappa Grossa 24', 'Stadt Winterthur', or an internal 'EMEA > CHE > ...' path), and addressRegion can hold a town, an internal path or prose - the parser normalises a trailing canton code, a trailing parenthetical, a '<town> - <street>' tail and a leading 'Stadt', maps the recognised canton spellings (German/French/English, incl. the board's 'Niderwalden' typo) onto the seeded CH-XX canton names, and rejects internal paths and prose rather than storing a bogus place. applicantLocationRequirements is a Country eligibility statement ('Switzerland'), NOT a remote signal, so it never sets a remote type; only an explicit jobLocationType TELECOMMUTE does (= remote_country). Capped runs always take the newest 120 rows (fresh_rows) plus a rotating slice of the tail whose start advances one budget-width per calendar day, so the oldest-first sitemap's older ads are covered over successive runs instead of the same first page being re-read forever. robots.txt (200, 2,217 bytes) advertises the sitemap and, for User-agent: *, disallows only /api/, /api_proxy/, /external/, /de|en|fr/application*, login/register, /fe/ktunnel/, /masks/, /javascript/, /*?*feat= and /*.map$ - none of which this scraper touches; no Crawl-delay is set, so a polite 1 s gap is kept. Switzerland had only jobs_ch (60 rows) before this source, and jobup.ch is not a duplicate: 8 of 15 sampled jobup.ch UUIDs resolved on none of the en/fr/de jobs.ch detail paths (all 404), so it carries meaningfully distinct postings. Scope added for this source: the 26 Swiss cantons in ref.regions (CH-XX codes) and 93 Swiss cities in ref.cities (on top of the pre-existing 'Zurich' row), plus SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['jobup_ch']='CH'. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

jobindex.dk (Jobindex, Denmark) - Denmark's largest commercial job board, and a distinct inventory from the state board jobnet_dk already in the corpus. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. robots.txt (HTTP 200) has a generic User-agent: * group with NO Crawl-delay; it disallows the paged/sorted/filtered search URLs (/jobsoegning*page=, *sort=, *jobage=, *archive=, *subid=, *supid=, *companyid=, *radius=, *flag=, *geoareaid=, /jobsoegning?*&*&, /jobsoegning/*?*&, /jobsoegning/kort, /jobsoegning/uopfordret, /jobsoegning/analyse), every /c? redirect link, and /jobannonce/korrektur/ and /jobannonce/embed/. The surfaces this scraper uses are all allowed: /jobsoegning, /jobsoegning/<area>, /sitemap/area.gz, /vis-job/<tid> and /jobannonce/<tid>/<slug>; a polite 0.25 s gap is kept anyway. Discovery is the board's ADVERTISED sitemap https://www.jobindex.dk/sitemap.gz (a <sitemapindex>) whose area.gz child is a <urlset> of 759 /jobsoegning/<slug> area pages; there is no job-ad sitemap (googleforjobs.gz is an EMPTY <urlset>, 0 <loc>, even as Googlebot, and company.gz/salaryindex.gz/content.gz hold company profiles, salary pages and articles). Each listing page embeds a large var Stash JSON object whose ['jobsearch/result_app/list']['storeData']['searchResponse'] carries hitcount, total_pages, max_page (50), page_size (20) and a results array of 20 ad objects (tid, headline, companytext, firstdate, lastdate, apply_deadline, salary, home_workplace, area, addresses, listlogo_url and the rendered snippet in html). The board held 18,829 active ads over a reported 942 pages on 2026-11-20, but page= is robots-DISALLOWED, so pages are never walked: the 759 allowed area pages are sampled in a rotating window and deduped by tid (a 20-area sample yielded 263 rows and 198 unique ads, so a full pass covers several thousand distinct ads and successive runs cover the long tail). Content is one request per ad when the snippet exposes the canonical /jobannonce/<tid>/<slug> URL, else one request to /vis-job/<tid> whose <link rel=canonical> is followed when it points at a /jobannonce/ page. The slug is required: a wrong or missing slug returns HTTP 200 with NO body, so only the slug from the snippet or the canonical link is used. Measured on 60 sampled ads: 15 (25%) have a full body in section.jobtext-jobad__body (1,708-8,149 chars, median 3,310) and 45 (75%) are employer-paid ads that publish only a 530-695 char teaser on Jobindex and link out to the employer, whose full text is NOT on this board; a teaser is stored as the description and flagged in raw_payload['description_source']='vis_job_teaser', and no external employer page is fetched. salary was null on all 116 sampled listing rows and the ad pages publish no salary field, so no amount is invented: rows state DKK/monthly. Employment type and remote work are published only on full-body pages, in the 'Virksomheden tilbyder' / 'The company offers' sidebar card (Ansættelsestype: Fastansættelse/Permanent/Freelance/Studiejob/Fleksjob; Hjemmearbejde: 100 % hjemmearbejde/100% remote/Tilbydes ikke/Ikke oplyst; Ugentlig arbejdstid: Fuldtid/Deltid (12-37 timer)); weekly hours is the more specific signal, and two or more different codes (Fuldtid, Deltid / Freelance, Studiejob) become no type rather than a guess. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['jobindex_dk']='DK' (Denmark is seeded as DK/DNK with default currency DKK) so an ad with no area still lands in Denmark. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

vdab.be (VDAB, Flanders' public employment service, Belgium) - the official Flemish vacancy database, a distinct inventory from any commercial Belgian board. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. robots.txt (HTTP 200) has a generic User-agent: * group with NO Crawl-delay; it disallows /vac/, /vacatures/, /api/vindeenjob/, /include/vacature/ and /*action=*/. The two surfaces used here carry no matching rule - the prefix /vacatures/ does not match /vindeenjob/vacatures/... - and the disallowed /api/vindeenjob/ base (applications, attachments) is never touched; the Angular ad pages are never fetched either, because everything comes from the REST API. A polite 0.25 s gap is kept anyway. Discovery is POST /rest/vindeenjob/v4/vacatureLight/zoek with {criteria:{onlineSindsCode:'9000',sorteerVeld:'DATUM'},pagina:N,zoekmodus:'C2',paginaGrootte:200} (~212,800 active ads on 2026-11-21), re-sorted locally by eerstePublicatieDatum desc then id desc so the window is deterministic; the newest 200 rows are always taken and the rest of the 500-ad budget comes from a window that advances one width per calendar day, so the tail is covered over successive runs instead of re-reading the same head. Detail is GET /rest/vindeenjob/v4/vacatures/<id>?preview=false, whose Schema.org jobPosting arrives as a JSON string. Every request sends the static vej-key-monitor correlation id shipped verbatim in the site's own chunk-CpGZcmxc.js; without it the API answers 403 with an empty body. It is a public front-end constant, not a credential. Description is functie.omschrijving.plainText (the markdown jobPosting.description and the HTML block are fallbacks), so no employer page is fetched. jobPosting.validThrough is a real closing date on ~6% of ads (12 of 200 sampled) and stays None otherwise. No salary field exists anywhere in the payload, so rows state EUR / monthly with salary_disclosed=False and no amount is invented. Employment type comes from functie.arbeidscircuit.code, with ordinary G/GC split full/part by profiel.dienstregeling.arbeidsDuur (V/D) and FL/WS/E left None because those codes have no honest ref.employment_types equivalent. The payload has no structured remote field (no jobLocationType, no telewerk facet), so remote work is a conservative Dutch/French phrase scan that defaults to on_site. apply_url is the board's own ad page; the employer's logischeLocatie.webadres is kept in raw_payload as external_apply_url because it is often a campaign redirect. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['vdab_be']='BE' (Belgium is seeded as BE/BEL with default currency EUR), so an ad whose place is a bare municipality still lands in Belgium. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

lexpress_mu (L'Express Petites Annonces, lexpress-petites-annonces.mu, Mauritius) - the classifieds arm of the island's main daily newspaper, whose Emplois category is a genuine jobs board (mostly employer postings) and a distinct inventory from the existing myjob MU source. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. The news host lexpress.mu only links to the sister host; the ads live on lexpress-petites-annonces.mu. robots.txt on both hosts (HTTP 200) is a generic User-agent: * group with an EMPTY Disallow (allow-all) and no Crawl-delay; a polite 0.5 s gap is kept anyway. Discovery is the server-rendered category /c/emplois, which paginates with ?page={n} (page 1 is the bare path, ~12 ads/page, 126+ ads across 11+ live pages on 2026-11-21); ad URLs are /annonce/- and the whole token is the stable source_job_id. Detail pages carry NO schema.org JSON-LD and NO employer/salary field: the fields are a handful of Tailwind paragraphs - title from

, a 'Ref: ' line, a breadcrumb 'Emplois > Full-Time|Part-Time' (the employment type is its tail), a French long-form date ('16 novembre 2026', read with a French month table because the shared English date parser cannot), the body in

, and a 'Localisation: ' line. The breadcrumb and the Localisation line share the exact class text-sm text-gray-500, distinguished by the breadcrumb containing '>'. and og:* are site-wide ('L'Express Petites Annonces') and never used as the job title. Salary, when stated at all, is prose in the body ('Salary Package: MUR 27,000 - MUR 35,000 per month.'); a MUR/Rs figure is parsed to min/max with the stated period, defaulting to monthly (the Mauritius convention, see myjob) and recording that assumption in raw_payload. Employer is best-effort: the ad's Google-Maps query when present, else a conservative '<Name> is looking/recruiting' body heuristic, else 'Unknown employer' (a classifieds board of anonymous ads is a property of the board, so this never fails the batch). Contact emails are Cloudflare-obfuscated (data-cfemail); the decoded address is recovered for audit. A remote-work phrase (teletravail/remote/...) is recorded in raw_payload but never mapped to a remote_work_type_code, because a classifieds line saying 'remote' never states how remote. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['lexpress_mu']='MU' (Mauritius is already seeded via myjob), so an ad naming only a local place ('Moka', 'Roches Noires') still lands in Mauritius. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

revolico_cu (Revolico, revolico.com, Cuba) - Cuba's large general classifieds site, whose Empleos category carries an employers' sub-board, 'Ofertas de Empleo' (the sibling 'Busco Empleo' holds job-seekers), that is a genuine jobs board: hundreds of employer postings, paginated about 100 to a page. Cuba had ZERO coverage before this source. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. robots.txt (HTTP 200) is a generic User-agent: * group that allows everything except /checkout/, /cdn-cgi/, /account, /auth and /favorites/, none of which are used; a polite 0.5 s gap is kept anyway. There is NO schema.org JSON-LD and NO separate API: each server-rendered Next.js page embeds its data in <script id="__NEXT_DATA__" type="application/json">, and the ads are the AdType:* entries of props.pageProps.__APOLLO_STATE__. Discovery is /search?category=empleos_&subcategory=empleos-ofertas-de-empleo; the subcategory slug ALONE returns an empty page and the numeric category id returns HTTP 500, so both params are required. Pagination is ?page={n} and page 1 is the bare path. Listings carry partial ads (no body), so one detail request is made per ad. Ad URLs are /item/<slug>-<id> and <id> is the stable source_job_id. There is NO employer field (the ad's name is the poster, kept as poster_name) and NO salary field: price/currency are unreliable (55 of 102 sampled ads carry none and many of the rest carry a placeholder 1), so no row is treated as a disclosed salary; both are kept in raw_payload and currency_iso_code is the home-market CUP with NO CUP rate added to salary_standardization.py. There is no original posting date, only updatedOnByUser (the last bump), whose date is used and flagged in raw_payload. Employer stays 'Unknown employer'. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=revolico_cu -> CU, so every ad lands in Cuba; no Cuban city is seeded (names like 'Florida' collide with seeded cities elsewhere). Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere).

timesjobs_in (TimesJobs, timesjobs.com, India) - India's long-running job board. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser: discovery is a keyless POST to tjapi.timesjobs.com/search/api/v1/search/jobs/list (JSON body keyword/location/experience/page/size/jobFunctions/company/industry/functionAreaId/jobFunction -> {total,page,size,totalPages,jobs}), newest-first by postDate, size accepts >=500, and every job is then hydrated by a keyless GET tjapi.timesjobs.com/job-api/api/jobs/public/<token> (token = the text after 'jobid-' in the listing jobDetailUrl, URL-encoded as one path segment). The public site's robots.txt (HTTP 200) is a generic User-agent: * group allowing everything except /timesJobWebApp/, /logout.html, /AutoLogin.html and /times_logout, none used; the API host tjapi.timesjobs.com serves NO readable robots.txt (/robots.txt and / both HTTP 502 from its nginx gateway) - the owner reviewed this and approved building on 2026-11-21, recording the 502 as an observed fact rather than treating it as permission, matching the api.p.hr.ge (404) / cupid.51job.com (400) / api.il.jobmaster.co.il (200) precedent. Salary is effectively hidden (hideCtcFromCandidate=true, minCtc/maxCtc=-1 on 30/30 sampled details) but a positive pair is still mapped; currency is INR, pay period yearly (annual CTC). Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=timesjobs_in -> IN.

xpress_jobs (XpressJobs, xpress.jobs, Sri Lanka) - Sri Lanka's general job board. The site is a React SPA (an empty 1.8 KB HTML shell on every path) served by nginx with no Cloudflare or bot wall, so its jobs come from a keyless public JSON API under /api/ rather than the DOM. No key, no registration, no cookie, no proxy, no browser; TLS verification stays on. robots.txt (HTTP 200, 114 bytes) is a single generic User-agent: * group whose Disallow: directive is EMPTY (everything is allowed) plus a Sitemap: line, and it has no Crawl-delay - /api/jobs/searchJobs and the /jobs/view/<id> ad pages are all allowed. Discovery is GET https://xpress.jobs/api/jobs/searchJobs, which returns a BARE JSON ARRAY (not an envelope) of listing rows; page is 1-based, pageSize is capped at 100 server-side, and sortBy=SortedCreateDate DESC (the public page's own 'Recent' option) is the only value that makes the feed deterministic and pageable - the default NEWID() re-randomises every call and would double-fetch. Each row carries recordCount (4,143 live ads on 2026-11-28). Each ad is then hydrated by GET https://xpress.jobs/api/jobs/publishedJob?jobId=<id>, which returns the full record: jobInfo (HTML body), education, experience, minSalary/maxSalary/salaryRange strings, sectors, the nested jobItem and the organization block. The public page is https://xpress.jobs/jobs/view/<id>. Salary is mostly hidden: the board answers 'Any' (or a placeholder 1) on most ads, and the cleaner treats both as undisclosed (salary_disclosed=false) while real whole-LKR figures pass through; currency LKR, pay_period monthly. jobType maps Full-Time/Permanent -> full_time, Contract Basis -> contract, Part-Time -> part_time, with Other and 'Full-Time or Part-Time' left NULL because they are unmappable. The bare remote boolean states no restriction level, so remote_work_type_code stays NULL; sectors are categories, not skills, so skills is empty and they stay in raw_payload. The listing's createdDate is always null; the detail's ISO createdDate is the posting date and expiryDateOnWebsite is the closing date. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=xpress_jobs -> LK (country_id 5634); only a handful of Sri Lankan cities are seeded, so an unseeded 'City, Province' string resolves to the country-level LK location through the fallback. Verified locally 2026-11-28: 200 fetched, 200 parsed, 200 cleaned, batch validation PASSED (0% skip), 200 inserted, 0 failed; 19 salary-disclosed (all LKR monthly), posting dates 2026-10-12..2026-11-27, descriptions 43-844 words (avg 240), 111 employers, employment full_time 183 / contract 11 / temporary 1 / none 5, all 200 rows resolved to Sri Lanka (138 Colombo, 23 Gampaha, 8 Kandy, 7 country-level and the rest other seeded cities; 0 null, 0 global-remote), closing date on 199, average data_quality_score 0.891. DISABLED IN CI: GitHub Actions run 46166163376 (api group, commit 78702d2, Scrape (API)) was answered HTTP 403 Forbidden -- the site's own nginx default body -- on GET https://xpress.jobs/api/jobs/searchJobs, so 0 postings were fetched and the run exited 1. The identical plain requests client with the same browser User-Agent is served 200 and hydrates 200/200 from a local/residential connection, so this is runner IP reputation, not the config. Proxies and keys are not permitted, so the source stays registered but disabled (enabled=false) rather than removed; it works when run locally and can be re-enabled when the runner block lifts.

zangia_mn (Zangia, zangia.mn, Mongolia) - Mongolia's long-running job board; its public search and detail are two keyless GETs on the HR API host, not server-rendered HTML. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. There is NO readable robots.txt anywhere on the property: zangia.mn, www.zangia.mn, hr-api.zangia.mn and new-api.zangia.mn all return HTTP 404 (no policy file exists) - the owner reviewed this and approved building on 2026-11-21, recording the 404s as an observed fact and relying on RFC 9309's allow-all posture for an absent robots.txt (matching the api.p.hr.ge 404 / cupid.51job.com 400 / api.il.jobmaster.co.il 200 / tjapi.timesjobs.com 502 precedent). Discovery is GET hr-api.zangia.mn/api/job/public/list/search ({data,page,limit,total,totalPages}; default 90/page, limit accepts >=500, newest-first by sortTime; 6,099 rows at scoping) and every listing row is hydrated by GET hr-api.zangia.mn/api/job/public/detail/<code> (the 200 envelope {data,message}; a bad code is a 404 'ES Job not found'). The listing row's 'code' is the URL slug (public page https://zangia.mn/job/<code>) and the stable source_job_id. Salary is always stated (salary{id,phrase,min,max}) in whole MNT quoted monthly; pay_period is monthly and currency is MNT. timetype.name_en is 'Full-time' or 'Shift' (Shift is a work schedule, not an employment type, so it is left unmapped). company.logo is an opaque code with no resolvable CDN URL, so company_logo_url is None. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=zangia_mn -> MN.

anpe_bf (ANPE/ABPE Burkina Faso, www.anpe.gov.bf, Burkina Faso) - the national employment agency's official site (now branded 'Agence Burkinabe Pour l'Emploi - Faso Tonlo Zi'); the old anpe.bf domain no longer resolves. It is a WordPress install and its public REST API is keyless: GET www.anpe.gov.bf/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?categories=77&per_page=100&page=N returns the site's own 'offres-demplois' category (X-WP-Total 97 at scoping, oldest 2024-09-13, newest 2026-07-03; one page). No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser; robots.txt (HTTP 200) is a generic User-agent: * group with Allow: / and no Disallow. Every post is one record ({id, date, modified, link, title.rendered, content.rendered, excerpt.rendered}) - there is NO structured salary, employer, location or contract field, so the cleaner lifts the prose signals it can: location is the first commune/mairie/province phrase (free text), and the contract wording maps CDI->full_time, CDD->contract, stagiaire/stage d'initiation->internship, temps partiel->part_time, with a bare 'stage' (usually 'attestation de stage') deliberately unmapped. Salary is NEVER stated anywhere in the category ('francs CFA' appears only in stamp-fee instructions), so salary_disclosed is always False and no bounds are invented; currency is XOF and pay_period takes the documented inert default (yearly) that the required-str model column forces. The employer is never a field, so company_name is the publishing agency and no client is guessed from the title. A minority of titles use Unicode mathematical-bold letters; NFKC normalizes them. The host is slow and occasionally drops a request, so the client retries timeouts/5xx with backoff (90s timeout, 4 attempts). Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=anpe_bf -> BF.

anpe_mali (ANPE Mali / Agence Nationale Pour l'Emploi, anpe-mali.org, Mali) - Mali's national employment agency ('Republique du Mali - Service public de l'emploi'); the old anpe.ml domain the earlier sweep recorded no longer resolves (NXDOMAIN) and anpe-mali.org is the live replacement. It is a WordPress install running the WP Job Manager plugin, and its public REST API is keyless: GET anpe-mali.org/wp-json/wp/v2/job-listings?per_page=100&page=N returns the job post type as a JSON array (X-WP-Total 15 at scoping, one page; the site's own sitemap wp-sitemap-posts-job_listing-1.xml lists the same 15 /poste/<slug>/ URLs, cross-checking the count). No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser; robots.txt (HTTP 200) is User-agent: * / Disallow: /wp-admin/ / Allow: /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, and the /wp-json/ path used here is not disallowed. _embed=wp:featuredmedia folds each listing's company logo into the same request, so there is no per-listing detail call. Each row is a full notice ({id, date, modified, link, slug, title.rendered, content.rendered, meta, job-types, job-categories, class_list}); meta carries the structured fields (_company_name, _job_location, _application, _remote_position, _job_salary). Location is free text ('Bamako' 8, 'Mali'/'MALI' 3, 'Sur site' 4, '' 1): 'Sur site' is a work arrangement, not a place, so it is dropped from location_cleaned and recorded as remote_work_type_code=on_site. The contract taxonomy is the class_list job-type-<slug>: cdi->full_time, cdd->contract, interim->temporary, independant->freelance, stage->internship; a multi-value row is left unset rather than guessed (job-types term ids are a fallback when class_list is absent). Salary is NEVER stated (meta._job_salary is empty on all 15), so salary_disclosed is always False and no bounds are invented; currency is XOF and pay_period takes the documented inert default (yearly) that the required-str model column forces. The employer IS a field (meta._company_name) and the logo comes from the embedded featured media. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=anpe_mali -> ML.

llv_li (Liechtensteinische Landesverwaltung / AVW, llv.li, Liechtenstein) - the official vacancies of the Principality's state administration. The LLV careers page /de/karriere/jobs links out to its SmartRecruiters board (careers.smartrecruiters.com/LiechtensteinischeLandesverwaltung); the board is server-rendered (7 postings at scoping) and every detail page lives on jobs.smartrecruiters.com/<company>/<id>-<slug> and carries schema.org microdata, so the generic HTML scraper framework reads it with plain HTTP - no key, no browser, no proxy. robots.txt: jobs.smartrecruiters.com/robots.txt -> HTTP 404 (no restrictions); careers.smartrecruiters.com/robots.txt -> an SPA HTML document with no robots directives; www.smartrecruiters.com/robots.txt is a real User-agent: * file that Disallows specific companies and does NOT list LiechtensteinischeLandesverwaltung. The JSON API host api.smartrecruiters.com returns robots User-agent: * / Disallow: /, so it is deliberately NOT used - only the HTML board and detail pages. Field map: title=og:title (the first h1 is an empty overlay header); company=meta[itemprop='name']; location=meta[itemprop='addressLocality'] (Vaduz/Schaan); description=.job-sections; posted_date=meta[itemprop='datePosted']; employment_type=li[itemprop='employmentType'] (Vollzeit/Teilzeit -> full_time/part_time); remote_work_type=spl-job-location[workplacetype] (on_site). Salary is never stated, so salary_disclosed is always False; currency CHF and pay_period monthly are inert defaults. base_url is jobs.smartrecruiters.com so the quality filter accepts the absolute detail URLs as same-site; detail_url_pattern .*/LiechtensteinischeLandesverwaltung/\d+-.* bypasses the path-keyword gate. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=llv_li -> LI.

bdjobs_com (Bdjobs, bdjobs.com, Bangladesh) - Bangladesh's largest job board. No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. robots.txt posture is what shaped this source: the two HTML hosts are both closed to a generic crawler - bdjobs.com/robots.txt (HTTP 200) declares a User-agent: * group that disallows a list of asset paths and then a SECOND User-agent: * group with Disallow: /, and RFC 9309 combines rules for the same user-agent, so the effective policy for * is disallow-all; jobs.bdjobs.com/robots.txt (HTTP 200) is the same shape. The API host is separate and open: api.bdjobs.com/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 (an IIS HTML not-found page, no policy file), which RFC 9309 treats as 'unavailable' and permits, the same allow-on-404 reading this repo applied to jobs.smartrecruiters.com for llv_li. Accordingly the scraper fetches ONLY api.bdjobs.com and never any bdjobs.com / jobs.bdjobs.com HTML page; the public https://bdjobs.com/h/details/<id> URL it stores is a link for humans, never a request. Discovery and data are the two keyless GETs the site's own SPA calls, copied verbatim from its bundled config chunk https://bdjobs.com/h/chunk-SMUS2CWI.js (keys searchEndpoint and detailsApiBaseUrl): GET api.bdjobs.com/jobs/api/v1/JobSearch/GetJobSearch?pg=N&rpp=100 returns {message,statuscode,data[],premiumData[],common{total_records_found,totalpages,total_vacancies}} (newest-first; ~5,747 rows over 58 pages at scoping) and data+premiumData are merged and de-duplicated by Jobid, and every row is hydrated by GET api.bdjobs.com/jobs/api/v1/JobSubsystem/jobDetails?jobId=<id>&ln=1&IsCorporate=false (a browser User-Agent is enough; no extra header needed). Field map: title=JobTitle/jobTitle; company=CompanyNameENG then the site's own misspelling CompnayName then companyName; description=JobDescription with AdditionJobRequirements, EducationRequirements and JobOtherBenifits folded in; skills=comma-split SkillsRequired plus SuggestedSkills; location=JobLocation/jobLocation; dates=ISO publishDate/deadlineDB and the human PostedOn/Deadline. Salary is often undisclosed: ShowSalary is '0' on some rows, many disclosed rows are 'Negotiable' (bounds 0), the rest carry 'Tk. <min> - <max> (Monthly)'; the cleaner maps positive BDT bounds, honours ShowSalary == 0 as a site-side withhold, and swaps a reversed pair; currency BDT and pay period monthly (the Bangladesh convention). JobNature (Full Time/Contractual/Part Time) maps to employment_type and JobWorkPlace (Work at office/Work from home/blank) maps to remote_work_type. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=bdjobs_com -> BD.

blmis_bt (BLMIS, blmis.gov.bt, Bhutan) - the Bhutan Labour Market Information System, the public job portal of Bhutan's labour ministry (MoLHR, whose functions now sit under MOICE; the site links to facebook.com/moicebt and twitter.com/MOLHRBhutan). This row's recorded domain, jobs.molhr, no longer exists: both molhr.gov.bt and jobs.molhr.gov.bt are NXDOMAIN at the .bt authoritative nameservers (dns.google/resolve, Status 3), so this is a successor build in the same spirit as llv_li, whose state vacancies had moved onto a SmartRecruiters board. No key, no registration, no login, no cookie, no proxy, no browser. robots.txt: https://www.blmis.gov.bt/robots.txt (HTTP 200) is a bare User-agent: * group with an EMPTY Disallow (allow-all) and no Crawl-delay. Data source: GET https://www.blmis.gov.bt/jobseeker_page/mispage ('Vacancies & Trainings') is a Laravel Livewire page that server-renders the current vacancy inventory into the component's wire:initial-data attribute (an HTML-entity-encoded JSON blob) before any JavaScript runs, so one plain GET is the whole source - no AJAX follow-up, no detail-page fetching. serverMemo.data carries six overlapping job_by_* browse facets (categories, location, company, qualification, yelp, oversea) over the SAME inventory; the client merges all six and de-duplicates by application_no (442 unique vacancies at scoping; job_by_company alone held 362). Field map: title=designation; company=company_name then business_name then the named placement for a domestic row with neither; description=job_description with qualification, eligible_criteria, terms_conditon (the site's spelling) and remarks folded in; location=gewog_name + dzongkhag_name (sub-district, district) for a domestic posting, or placement (the destination country) for an overseas one; posted_date=created_at ('2026-11-19 09:23:25'); closing_date=last_date_registration ('2026-12-10'); employment_type=employment_type (Regular -> full_time, Contract -> contract); salary=starting_salary, a single monthly figure with no range and no currency code, stored as salary_min with salary_max left honestly unstated (0/absent -> undisclosed). Currency is BTN (ngultrum) for domestic rows; an overseas row (vacancy_type_id 516) quotes the destination currency, mapped from the placement country (Qatar -> QAR) with a BTN fallback. There is no skills or work-mode field, so those stay empty/None rather than guessed. The stored original_url is the public detail page https://www.blmis.gov.bt/jobseeker_page/jobdetails/<application_no>, a link for humans that is never fetched (that route returns only the SPA shell). Seeded alongside this build: ref.countries now has Bhutan (BT) and ref.currencies now has BTN. Certificate verification stays ON (no verify=False). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=blmis_bt -> BT.

Detail is two keyless GETs per job: (1) structured GET https://bongthom.com/Job_Controller/get_embed/<id> returns positions[] each with an HTML description, duties[].text, benefits[].benefit, skill_knowledges[].skill, categories[].name_en, qualifications[].major and experiences[] with numeric years; (2) rendered GET https://bongthom.com/job_detail/view_detail_<id>.html renders the 'Workplace Circumstances' list, the only place the displayed work location, salary and schedule appear (get_embed leaves schedule/salary null for most rows and its locations objects are legacy office addresses, not the work site). Field map: title/company/logo from the embed (discovery row as fallback, the error_pic logo placeholder dropped); description folds the position descriptions, duties, benefits, qualifications and experience bullet text; skills = skill_knowledges[].skill cleaned/lowercased/deduped; experience_years_min = min(experiences[].years); location = the rendered Location value(s) joined by '; '; salary = the rendered Salary value ($<min> - $<max> or a lone $<value>, else Negotiable/Based on Experience/N/A/Other Benefits -> undisclosed); employment = the rendered Schedule value (Full-time/Part-time/Short-term mapped to full_time/part_time/temporary; a combined label left unmapped). Salary is USD (Cambodia's dollarised economy) and monthly. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=bongthom_com -> KH; ref.countries needed a Cambodia row (added alongside). The rendered page writes every label/value row into li.clearfix.en regardless of display language (a Khmer-default posting puts Khmer label text in the same class), so the parser keeps a row only when its strong label is a known English label.

Kariyer.net (www.kariyer.net) - Turkiye; the country's largest generalist private-sector board, the private-market counterpart to the state portal iskur_gov_tr. No key, no registration, no login, no cookie, no proxy; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False). The www marketing HTML sits behind HUMAN/PerimeterX (app id PXqzR3QUY9) and hard-403s a non-browser client, but the board's own SPA publishes two PUBLIC JSON gateways that are NOT behind that interstitial, and both host names appear verbatim in the site's JavaScript bundle: search POST https://candidatewebapigw.kariyer.net/jb/api/jobs/search (body {pageNumber, pageSize}) and detail GET https://api-web.kariyer.net/job?jobId=<id> (the bundle's VUE_APP_API_DOMAIN_V1; its VUE_APP_API_V4_DOMAIN twin candidatesearchapigateway.kariyer.net serves the identical document but is PX-fronted and intermittently 403s, so it is kept as detail_fallback_base_url and the client tries it only when the mirror fails). Both calls speak through curl_cffi with impersonate=chrome: the search gateway answers plain requests but the detail gateways reject their TLS fingerprint, so the whole client uses curl_cffi (the same fix JobsNepal and Job.am use). The detail call must NOT send Api-Version (adding 1.1 turns a 200 into a 403) and the request carries Origin/Referer https://www.kariyer.net/. robots.txt (HTTP 200): the generic User-agent: * group disallows /filtre*, *?v=, *?ckw*, *?copilot* and the candidate/account paths, and ALLOWS /is-ilanlari (the listing) and /is-ilani/ (the ad pages); the scraper requests no disallowed path and links back to the allowed /is-ilani/<slug>-<id> ad URL. Discovery is the search gateway's pageNumber windows, but a requested pageSize caps at ~53 rows and the windows OVERLAP AND ROTATE, so de-duplicating by jobId is mandatory, not an optimisation (measured 2026-11-22: 22,696 total ads, page 1 returned 53 items). Each ad's detail document (data.jobGeneralInformation / jobPositionInformation / jobCandidateCriteria / jobCompanyInformation) supplies the HTML body (qualificationsWithHtml, plain fallback qualifications), ISO postingDate, closingDateNumeric (dd.mm.yyyy), locations[], workType/workTypeText, workModel, positionLevelText and the education/experience criteria. TRAPS: (1) jobSalaryBudget is null on every TR ad sampled, so pay reads undisclosed in TRY with pay_period=monthly (a required column); (2) educationLevelText is a LIST of EVERY level the ad accepts, ordered lowest first, so the requirement is the MINIMUM across the list (a ['Lise(Mezun)',...,'Yuksek Lisans(Mezun)'] ad is a high-school role, not a master's); (3) locality is written with Turkish letters and a side marker ('Istanbul(Asya)'), which the shared resolver cannot match against its ASCII ref.cities seed, so location_cleaned folds Turkish letters to ASCII and drops the parenthetical, letting 'Istanbul' resolve to city_id 41 (only Turkish city seeded); SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=kariyer_net -> TR (country_id 25 'Turkey', default_currency_id 23 TRY) keeps the country on a non-Istanbul posting. Turkiye had only ONE source before this (iskur_gov_tr), so this is a large net-new country/board.

Nationale Vacaturebank (www.nationalevacaturebank.nl) - Netherlands; one of the country's largest generalist job boards (DPG Media) and the first large plain-request HTML source for NL. A fresh session's first HTML response can be the 'DPG Media Privacy Gate' consent wall (~8 KB); simply re-requesting the same URL on the same session (the first GET sets the authId/xAuthId cookies) returns the real page, which is what the client's consent seed does - the gate's own /privacygate-confirm callback 403s and is never called. robots.txt (HTTP 200) generic User-agent: * group: DISALLOWS /vacatures/*?page= (and /vacatures/*?*&page=), /vacature/zoeken?*, /vacature/uitgebreid-zoeken, /vacature/bookmarken/, /vacature/delen/, /vacature/apply/, /vacature/external-url/, /vacature/website/, /vacature/bladeren/, /archief/, /zzp/, /werkgever/... and /recruiter/; ALLOWS the surfaces this scraper reads: /vacatures, the category pages under /vacatures/vakgebied|branche|provincie|dienstverband|uren|opleiding/, the published /vacatures/sitemap.xml and the /vacature/<uuid>/<slug> ad pages. The API host api.nationalevacaturebank.nl/robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /' and is NEVER requested. Discovery: the board's own /vacatures/sitemap.xml lists 241 category URLs; the scraper keeps the 91 content categories and walks a rotating window of 4 per run (rotation_slot_hours=12, aligned with this group's schedule), reading PAGE 1 ONLY of each because ?page= is disallowed; no query string is ever appended. Ad links are merged round-robin across the selected categories and de-duplicated by UUID. Each ad page (~95-110 KB) publishes a schema.org JobPosting block with title, hiringOrganization.name, jobLocation.address (addressLocality/addressRegion/addressCountry/postalCode + lat/lon), datePosted, validThrough, employmentType, educationRequirements.credentialCategory, experienceRequirements.monthsOfExperience, workHours, occupationalCategory, industry, jobLocationType, directApply, description and baseSalary. TRAPS: (1) datePosted/validThrough are stamped at 22:00Z/23:00Z (midnight NL), so both are converted to Europe/Amsterdam before the date is taken (raw UTC dates every ad one day early); (2) baseSalary is the ad's OWN offer and was present on 31 of 40 ads sampled (EUR, unitText MONTH in that sample; HOUR also seen) and is stored as salary_min/max + salary_disclosed, while a second Occupation block's estimatedSalary is the board's MARKET ESTIMATE and is kept in raw_payload only, never mapped; (3) an ad with no baseSalary is stored salary-undisclosed in EUR with pay_period=monthly (the Dutch convention, and a required column); (4) employmentType is usually the list ['FULL_TIME','PART_TIME'], the board's 'either' default, so a code is assigned only when the list resolves to exactly one type (INTERN->internship, CONTRACTOR->contract, TEMPORARY->temporary) and a mixed list stays None; (5) withdrawn ads answer HTTP 410 or a 200 with no JobPosting block and are counted and skipped, and a run that finds no live ad at all raises; (6) only ONE Dutch city is seeded in ref.cities, so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=nationalevacaturebank_nl -> NL is what keeps every other town (Groningen, Amersfoort, Emmen, ...) on the Netherlands instead of the shared global-remote location. The JobPosting block is read from server-rendered HTML, not a browser. Local dry run 2026-11-22: 4 categories, 200 ad links discovered, 60 fetched, 60 parsed, 60 cleaned, 0 withdrawn, 0 failures, batch validation PASSED. CI verification 2026-11-22 (Scrape (HTML) workflow_dispatch, run 45026658755): 60 fetched, 60 inserted, 0 failed, batch validation PASSED.

National Employment Agency (www.nea.gov.kh) - Cambodia's state employment portal (run under the Ministry of Labour) and the first government source in the corpus for Cambodia, a distinct inventory from the existing camhr_com and bongthom_com sources. No key, no registration, no login, no cookie, no proxy; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False). Transport is curl_cffi with impersonate=chrome: the bare root / answers a Cloudflare JS-challenge shell (~1.7 KB) to a non-browser client, but the content paths this scraper reads (/index.do, /vacancy/dtlSearch.do, /vacancy/view.do) are ordinary server-rendered HTML, and the bare root is NEVER requested, so no challenge is handled or bypassed. The 2026-10-04 sweep's 'SELENIUM/PLAYWRIGHT REQUIRED (headless browser) ... cf=True' verdict was measured on that bare root only. robots.txt (https://www.nea.gov.kh/robots.txt, HTTP 200) is the Cloudflare-managed generic User-agent: * group with Allow: / (plus a Content-Signal line: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference); the later training-crawler groups (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, ...) do not name this scraper's ordinary browser User-Agent and none restricts /vacancy/. Discovery is a POST of the board's own search form to /vacancy/dtlSearch.do (condDiv=SEARCH, condText='', condSort='', currentPageNo=N): ten rows per page, each navigating via fnVacancyViewNew('<32 hex>'); the board reported 654 vacancies on 2026-11-22 (~66 pages) and this scraper reads the first six pages per run (60 detail pages). Detail is GET /vacancy/view.do?condSeq=<32 hex> (~60-72 KB, no schema.org block): title in #vacancyTitle, employer in the first .tit_box span.tit, a summary block of .cont > strong.tit + span.con pairs, and labelled sections in .form_wrap (.form_title h3 + .view_form strong.title + p.cont_box/div.cont_box). TRAPS: (1) U+200B zero-width spaces are embedded inside Khmer words, so labels are normalised (invisibles stripped) before matching and values are cleaned; (2) the Khmer address row (the 'address' label) appears TWICE - the employer's address in the summary block and the JOB CENTRE's address near the bottom - and only the first non-empty value (the employer's) is used; (3) the Khmer 'number of workers required / workplace' summary row encodes the workplace as '<vacancies> / <province>', so the province after the slash is the location and the full employer address is the fallback; (4) salaries are USD per month (sampled Khmer 'month' + '$180~$250' and '$210~$250'), the dollar sign being Cambodia's quoting convention rather than a currency conversion, so the currency is USD and pay_period is always monthly even when no amount is published; (5) the Khmer recruitment-period row reads 'dd/mm/yyyy ~ dd/mm/yyyy' - start = posting date, end = closing date, and a literal 00/00/0000 is discarded; (6) the description section is frequently the literal placeholder 'Job Descriptions Responsibilities Duties' (38 chars), so a factual description is composed from the structured fields rather than shipping the placeholder; (7) ambiguous Khmer education ('has not yet finished university', a candidate statement rather than a completed level) is deliberately left unmapped while unambiguous degrees map, and 'no experience required' maps to 0 years -> entry. Cambodia (KH) is seeded (country_id 7573, country_name 'Cambodia'; USD is the dollarised market currency) but ref.cities holds NO Cambodian city at all, so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['nea_gov_kh'] = 'KH' is what keeps every province on Cambodia instead of the shared global-remote location. Verified locally 2026-11-22: 60 fetched, 0 failures, 60 parsed, 60 cleaned, batch validation PASSED. Verified in CI 2026-11-22 (Scrape (HTML) workflow_dispatch, run 45036048939): 60 fetched, 0 fetch failures, 60 parsed, 60 inserted, 0 failed, batch validation PASSED. The NEA origin is slow (~20 s per detail request), which is why the CI timeout is 60 minutes.

OCC Mundial (www.occ.com.mx) - Mexico's largest job board and the first Mexican source in the corpus. No key, no login, no proxy, no TLS bypass (no verify=False). robots.txt (https://www.occ.com.mx/robots.txt, HTTP 200) is the generic User-agent: * group: it disallows /rest and the account/help paths and allows /rest?server=jobs|jobProfiles|relatedSearches; /empleos/ (the listing this scraper reads) is not restricted. The listing is behind a Cloudflare managed challenge that plain HTTP answers with a 403/shell; an undetected Chrome (seleniumbase UC, headless) clears it in about five seconds, so the browser framework's client is used for the LISTING ONLY. Discovery cannot be anchor-based: every result is <li class='vacancy-card' data-id='...'> and the card navigates with JavaScript, so there is no <a href> to follow; instead each rendered listing page publishes a well-formed schema.org ItemList JSON-LD block whose itemListElement[].url values are the canonical ads. Up to four listing pages are read per run (18-20 cards per page; pagination observed to page 499). Detail is browserless: GET https://oferta.occ.com.mx/offer/<id>/d/j?ipo=41&iapo=1 via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome returns HTTP 200 JSON with no challenge and no auth; the ipo/iapo params are required or the endpoint 404s. The payload's o.* fields are mapped through the shared HTML framework's mapped_json_html: t=title, cn=company, c/l=locality/state, ld=description HTML, st=posted date, lset=employment type ('Tiempo completo' -> full_time), smin/smax=monthly MXN salary. The page's own JobPosting JSON-LD is NOT used: it is PascalCase and ends in a stray ';', so json.loads rejects it. TRAPS: (1) a hidden salary is published as smin=smax=0, not as a missing field, so the pair is nulled before mapping or a bogus '0 - 0' band would be stored; (2) the canonical ad URL is o.ur and carries a long tracking query, stripped for storage; (3) the ItemList URLs double the slash after the host (//empleo/...), normalized at discovery. Mexico is seeded (country_id 3, currency MXN) but ref.cities holds only a handful of Mexican cities, so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['occ_com_mx']='MX' keeps ads whose locality/state segments match no seeded city on Mexico instead of the shared global-remote location. Verified locally 2026-11-22: 60 fetched, 0 failures, 60 parsed, 60 cleaned, batch validation PASSED, 60 inserted, 0 failed. Verified in CI 2026-11-22 (Scrape (browser), run 45041534225, max_jobs=20): 20 fetched, 0 fetch failures, 20 parsed, 20 inserted, 0 failed, batch validation PASSED. This source runs ACTIVE in CI.

OLX.uz (olx.uz, Uzbekistan) - Uzbekistan; No key, no registration, no proxy, no browser. OLX Uzbekistan is a large classifieds job board, a second inventory beside the state portal (ish.mehnat.uz, still unreachable) and hh_uz. robots.txt (HTTP 200) is the generic User-agent: * group: it disallows */search/, */rss/, */api/v1/offers/metadata/, */api/v1/offers/*/suggested/, */api/v1/offers/*/page-views/, */api/v1/targeting/ and the account paths, and ends with 'Allow: /'; /rabota/ (the listing this scraper reads) is not restricted. TRAP: a plain requests client gets HTTP 403 (len 919) on BOTH /rabota/ and robots.txt -- this is the 2026-10-04 'HTTP 403 with anti-bot signals' verdict -- but it is a TLS/UA fingerprint block, not a challenge: curl_cffi with impersonate='chrome' returns HTTP 200 on the listing and detail pages, so no browser is needed. The listing is server-rendered HTML: https://www.olx.uz/rabota/ carries ~52 job-detail anchors per page, and pagination is the pager's own '?page={page}' query (pages 1 and 2 each returned 52 distinct ads). job_link is a[href*='/obyavlenie/rabota/'] and detail_url_pattern 'ID[0-9a-zA-Z]+\.html' keeps only the posting URLs; id_from_url + id_url_regex '(ID[0-9a-zA-Z]+)\.html' make the board's own 'IDxxxxxx' token the stable source_job_id. Each ad page publishes a full schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD, which detail_json_ld reads: title=title, company=hiringOrganization.name (frequently 'confidential', a real signal, kept verbatim), location=jobLocation.address.addressLocality + addressRegion + addressCountry ('UZ'), description=description, posted_date=datePosted, employment_type=employmentType, and the pay comes from the structured baseSalary (detail_json_salary: currency=baseSalary.currency, min/max from baseSalary.value.minValue/maxValue). OLX.uz's baseSalary.value has NO unitText, so pay_period falls back to the board default 'monthly' (all observed salaries are monthly; two ads state USD, and the ad's own currency overrides the board's UZS for those two). UZBEKISTAN IS SEEDED (country_id 3851, currency UZS id 3570) but ref.cities holds NO Uzbek city at all, so SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY['olx_uz']='UZ' is what pins every ad to Uzbekistan; the Cyrillic locality stays as raw text ('Tashkent, UZ'). A UZS->USD reference rate was added so normalized_annual_* are populated. Verified locally 2026-11-22: 60 fetched, 0 fetch failures, 53 parsed, 7 dropped for terse descriptions (under 80 chars), 53 cleaned, batch validation PASSED, 53 inserted, 0 failed; 53/53 rows resolved to Uzbekistan, 51 in UZS + 2 in USD, 41 full_time / 12 temporary. Pracuj.pl (www.pracuj.pl) - Poland; the largest Polish job board, a source distinct from the already-built praca_pl and olx_pl. Both the homepage and robots.txt answer Cloudflare's managed challenge ('Just a moment...') to plain requests and to curl_cffi under every browser profile, so this is a BROWSER source on the generic browser framework (scripts/run_browser_scraper.py, SeleniumBase undetected Chrome, uc_mode); TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False), no key, no login, no cookie, no proxy. A real undetected Chrome clears the challenge in about 10-16 s. robots.txt, read through the cleared browser, is a generic User-agent: * group that only disallows asset/account paths (/_styles/, /_scripts/, /_images/, /_images-app/, /templates/, /_includes/, /_files/, /L/, /l/, /konto/, /mpimages/, /oferty-loga-firm/, /kompendium-hr/files|images/, /e-pracodawcy/files|images/, /e-praktyki/files|images/) and points at the /SiteMaps/ index; /praca and the ,oferta, ad pages are allowed. Discovery walks the general feed /praca (listing_ready_selector a[href*=',oferta,']) with ?pn={page}; note that ?page=2 silently returns page 1 while ?pn=2 is the real pagination. Ad URLs are /praca/<slug>,oferta,<numeric id> and the id is the trailing digits. Each ad publishes a schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block whose @context key is literally '@content' (a site quirk the JSON-LD reader tolerates); fields come from detail_json_map: title, hiringOrganization (always a bare string in a 10/10 sample), jobLocation.address.addressLocality + addressRegion + addressCountry (e.g. 'Warszawa, mazowieckie, Polska'), and the body from description plus responsibilities/experienceRequirements/jobBenefits, because description is null on about four ads in five. datePosted drives posting_date and employmentType carries the Polish contract name (umowa o prace, kontrakt B2B, umowa o staz / praktyki); the shared cleaner does not map Polish contract names, so employment_type is NULL, as on praca_pl. detail_json_salary reads baseSalary.currency/minValue/maxValue/value/unitText; about a third of ads disclose pay, in PLN monthly (the board itself labels an hourly-looking 28.70 zl as '/ mies.'), so pay_period is monthly and currency PLN. Rendered pages keep a Cloudflare challenge-platform script even after the challenge clears, so ignore_challenge_markers='challenge-platform' and uc_reconnect_seconds=0 (uc_open_with_reconnect made the challenge repeat); inter_request_delay_seconds=2.0, max 60 ads over 3 listing pages. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=pracuj_pl -> PL; Poland (PL, country_id 19) and PLN (currency_id 19) are already seeded. ref.cities seeds only one Polish city ('Warsaw') and no Polish region spellings, so the resolver's country fallback (match_method=source_default_country) puts every ad on the shared country-level PL location row (location_id 98, raw text 'Remote, Poland', shared with praca_pl/olx_pl); the job's own remote_work_type_id stays NULL, so no ad is claimed remote. Local full run 2026-11-22: 60 fetched, 0 fetch failures, 60 parsed, 60 cleaned, batch validation PASSED, 60 inserted, 0 failed; 60/60 country PL, currency PLN monthly, 21 ads with a salary (min 28.70 / max 16,000.00 PLN), posting dates 2026-05-22..2026-11-22.

Robota.ua (https://robota.ua) - Ukraine; the largest Ukrainian job board, and Ukraine's first source on the platform. No key, no login, no proxy. The public website is behind Cloudflare (plain requests get HTTP 403 'Just a moment...' even for robots.txt), so every call goes through curl_cffi impersonating Chrome; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False anywhere). The API host's own robots.txt (https://dracula.robota.ua/robots.txt, HTTP 200) is a generic User-agent: * group that only disallows /swagger, /ui and /playground, so /graphql is allowed. Discovery and detail are one unauthenticated GraphQL query at https://dracula.robota.ua/graphql (the graphqlApi value in the site's Angular bundle): publishedVacancies(filter:{...}, sort:BY_DATE, pagination:{page,count}) returns totalCount and items carrying title, full HTML description, salary, company, city/region, schedules, subrubrics, employment and work types. totalCount was 97,981 on 2026-11-28; 100 items per page were accepted, pages did not overlap, and 12 rapid queries showed no rate limiting. salary is {amount, amountFrom, amountTo, comment, isNet, currency} with currency an ISO string (UAH observed): amountFrom/amountTo are the range, a single-value ad fills amount, a missing or non-positive bound is undisclosed (never invented), and pay is quoted monthly. workTypes are REMOTE/HYBRID/OFFICE -> remote_country/hybrid/on_site (the board is Ukraine-only, so REMOTE is country-scoped); employmentTypes are FULL_TIME/PART_TIME/PROJECT_BASED/SHIFT -> full_time/part_time/contract/(None: SHIFT is a schedule), and a multi-valued list with no single mapping stays None with the raw value in raw_payload. subrubrics become lowercased skills/tags. posting_date is firstPublishedAt (7-digit fractional seconds handled), falling back to createdAt then sortDate; there is no expiry field, so closing_date is NULL. company.name and company.logoUrl populate the employer; an anonymous ad becomes 'Confidential Employer'. The canonical URL is https://robota.ua/vacancy/{id}. Capped runs walk newest-first and skip already-stored source_job_ids, so a 200-ad window makes progress across the 97k board; max_pages=20 caps the walk. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=robota_ua -> UA (Ukraine seeded as UA/UKR, country_id 24; UAH seeded as currency_id 41) so a remote ad keeps its country. Local dry run 2026-11-28: 5 fetched, 5 parsed, 5 cleaned, batch validation PASSED, 0 failures.

The listing is server-rendered (plain requests get it), but every ad page answers HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge to plain requests and to curl_cffi impersonating chrome/chrome110/chrome120/safari17_0/edge101/firefox133, so this is a BROWSER source (SeleniumBase undetected Chrome, scripts/run_browser_scraper.py); UC with a 4 s reconnect clears the challenge and renders the ad. Discovery walks https://www.skywalker.gr/el/aggelies-ergasias?page={page} (page 1 bare), 25 ads per page with a pager through page 6; ad links are /el/aggelia-ergasias//, the ULID is the stable source_job_id (id_url_regex), and /apply and the 'small ads' (/el/mikri-aggelia-ergasias/) links are excluded. label

value

, which no stable class addresses -- the selectors use soupsieve :has(h5:-soup-contains(label)) to read the value beside each Greek label (company, posting date, employment type, work model, category). Location is the .plirofories-aggelias badge (a Greek municipality or region name). title_priority is 'selector,og:title' because the page's h1 is the generic site heading. The page carries a passive reCAPTCHA widget (g-recaptcha) and a Cloudflare challenge-platform script, so ignore_challenge_markers names both. A recent-ads RSS feed exists at /el/xml/aggelies-ergasias (allowed) but carries only a ~150-character teaser, so the ad pages are read for the full body. Employment type, work model and category are Greek words; ref.employment_types/ref.remote_work_types/ref.job_categories have no Greek mapping, so those codes stay NULL rather than being guessed (the same as the Estonian tootukassa_ee). No ad published a salary on the sampled ads, so no amount is invented; rows carry currency EUR and period monthly as a statement about the market. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=skywalker_gr -> GR (Greece is already seeded, High confidence) so a nominal location keeps its country. Snagajob (www.snagajob.com) - United States; the largest US hourly-work board (roughly 150k open hourly jobs), a source distinct from the already-built usajobs (federal) and builtin (tech). The homepage, listing and even robots.txt answer Cloudflare's 'Just a moment...' challenge to plain requests and to curl_cffi under every browser profile, so this is a BROWSER source on the generic browser framework (scripts/run_browser_scraper.py, SeleniumBase undetected Chrome, uc_mode); TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False), no key, no login, no cookie, no proxy. A real undetected Chrome clears the challenge (uc_reconnect_seconds=4). robots.txt, read through the cleared browser, is a generic User-agent: * group that allows the /find-jobs/<filter> section fronts and the /jobs/<id> ad pages and disallows only account/apply paths and every paginated or query-string URL (/find-jobs?*page=*, /find-jobs/page-*, /search?q=*, the /find-jobs/c-*,w-*,x-* combos, /profiles/, ...). Because pagination is disallowed, discovery walks the bare /find-jobs plus a fixed set of 37 allowed section fronts (the 12 industry i-* fronts and 25 job-type t-* fronts) via the new BrowserSiteConfig.listing_paths list, taking each front's first page and de-duplicating the ad links across every seed. Posted: 2026-11-27 Job Title: ...'), and employment type plus pay from the ad's own summary table rows found with soupsieve :has(th:-soup-contains(...)) ('Hours' -> full_time/part_time, 'Estimated Pay' -> e.g. '$14 per hour'). salary_text_regex reads the hourly '$N per hour' text into salary_min and salary_unit_text=HOUR (about a third of ads disclose pay); pay_period defaults to hourly and currency to USD, and the ad's own unit overrides the default. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=snagajob_com -> US; the United States (country_id 1) is already seeded, so an ad whose street-plus-town location resolves to no seeded city still keeps its country instead of collapsing onto the shared global-remote row.
