Subito.it (www.subito.it) - Italy; the country's largest general classifieds board, whose Lavoro e servizi section carries about 37,000 live offerte-lavoro listings (probe 2026-11-28). It sits behind Akamai: plain requests, robots.txt included, get HTTP 403 'Access Denied' from errors.edgesuite.net, while curl_cffi impersonating Chrome gets 200, so this is an HTML-framework source (scripts/run_html_scraper.py) with impersonate=chrome; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False), no key, no login, no proxy. robots.txt is a generic User-agent: * group whose only rules are Disallows (/ai?preselect, /pr/, /ai/verify/, /vf/, the PayPal paths, /annunciutente*, /lim?, /li?, /vim/, /vi/, /hades/ and every paginated URL *?o=* and *&o=*); the leading anti-automation comment is not an RFC 9309 directive (comments are ignored), so only the Disallow lines bind. Because the ?o= pager is disallowed, discovery never paginates: it walks page 1 of the national /annunci-italia/vendita/offerte-lavoro/ front plus one offerte-lavoro front per region (20 fronts) via the new SiteConfig.listing_paths list, de-duplicating ads across every seed by canonical URL. The listing renders no anchors server-side but ships the whole payload in __NEXT_DATA__ (props.pageProps.initialState.items.originalList, 30 ads per front); each AdItem already carries the full posting so no detail fetch happens: title=subject, company=advertiser.name (blank on some ads; 27 of the 60 stored rows became 'Unknown employer'), location=geo.town.value + geo.city.value + geo.region.value, employment_type=features./contract_type.values[].value, description=body (75-1,988 chars, avg about 1,223), posted_date=date. The stable source_job_id is the numeric ad id in the URL (id_url_regex -(\d+)\.htm$) and urls.default is the canonical ad URL. SALARY IS DELIBERATELY NOT MAPPED: the offerte-lavoro feed publishes no price on any sampled ad, so pay stays undisclosed rather than guessed; currency is EUR and pay_period monthly for ads that mention pay in the body. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=subito_it -> IT; Italy (country_id 10) is already seeded but its towns are not in ref.cities, so every ad folds into the existing country-level Italy location row (location_id 575) with the per-ad town/province/region preserved in core.location_aliases; all 60 rows carry country IT instead of collapsing onto the shared global-remote row. Local run 2026-11-28: 30 ads on the national front and 30 on the first region front (26 new after de-duplication), 60 fetched, 60 parsed, 60 inserted, batch validation PASSED, 0 failures, 8 employer rows, all 60 dated 2026-11-28.

Talent.com (www.talent.com) - global job aggregator, US English edition; robots.txt (HTTP 200, 2,039 B) is a generic User-agent: * group that allows the /jobs/<filter> landing fronts and the /view?id=<id> ad pages and disallows only the internal search APIs and redirector paths (/search-jobs/*, /services/api-new/search, /api/, /api/v1/tracker/pixel, /coreg/register.php, /neuvooEmailPixel, /cdn-cgi/rum, /redirect*, /convert*, /*.shtml, /invoice-report*, /ajax/*). Plain requests with the framework's honest research User-Agent get HTTP 200 on both the fronts and the ad pages: no key, no login, no cookie, no proxy, TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False) and no browser impersonation is needed. Discovery walks page 1 of nine keyword fronts (/jobs/k-engineer, k-nurse, k-driver, k-accountant, k-teacher, k-warehouse, k-sales, k-developer, k-administrative-assistant) and collects the /view?id=<digits> ad links, de-duplicated across seeds; the ?p=N pager is allowed but deliberately not used, so a run costs nine listing requests plus sixty ad fetches. The numeric ad id in the query string is the stable source_job_id and detail_url_pattern recognizes /view as an ad page rather than a section path. Ad pages are server-rendered: title from h1, employer and location from the companyLocationRow spans, body from jobDescriptionContainer (observed 1,730-10,307 chars, median about 3,600). Salary and employment type come from the visible label rows 'Salary' and 'Job type' via detail_label_map, with salary_text_regex reading '$39.55 hourly' and '$78,000.00 yearly' (comma thousands are collapsed by the shared _salary_number helper, extended in this pass); the page's schema.org JobPosting block fills datePosted for the roughly one third of ads that publish it, because the markup itself prints only a relative '4 days ago' that the generic parser cannot turn into a date, and those rows fall back to the scrape date. The US English edition is collected, so the rows are US jobs; SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY maps talent_com to US so that ads whose city is not seeded resolve to the country-level United States row instead of the shared global-remote location (seeded city names still resolve to their exact city; the entry must be removed if non-US editions are added later). Local dry run 2026-11-28: 60 fetched, 60 parsed, 0 skipped, batch validation PASSED, 30 distinct employers; local run 2026-11-28: 60 inserted, 0 failed.

TopCV (www.topcv.vn) - Vietnam's largest job board; robots.txt (HTTP 200, 337 B, server: cloudflare) is a generic User-agent: * group that disallows only the CV-builder and private paths (/cv/get-private-url/, /private/, /xem-cv/, /xem-cv-draft/, /sua-cv/, /viet-cv/, /edit/cv/, /cv-ung-vien/, /cv-ung-tuyen/, /p/ and one static png) and allows both the category listing fronts (the /tim-viec-lam-* search pages) and the ad pages (/viec-lam/<slug>/<id>.html); there is no Crawl-delay. The site sits behind Cloudflare: plain requests and every chrome/edge curl_cffi profile answer HTTP 403 ('Attention Required! | Just a moment...'), while curl_cffi impersonating Safari (safari17_0) gets HTTP 200, so this is an HTML-framework source (scripts/run_html_scraper.py) with impersonate=safari17_0; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False), no key, no login, no cookie, no proxy. Cloudflare also rate-limits: after roughly 15-20 ad fetches the IP starts receiving HTTP 429, which the client retries (2s then 4s) and, when that is still not enough, drops that one ad; a 4s inter-request delay keeps local runs at 55-59 of 60. Discovery walks page 1 of nine category search fronts (/tim-viec-lam-cong-nghe-thong-tin, -kinh-doanh, -marketing, -ke-toan, -hanh-chinh-nhan-su, -xay-dung, -san-xuat, -giao-duc-dao-tao, -kho-van) via listing_paths, collecting the /viec-lam/<slug>/<id>.html ad links; one front already yields about 50 ads, so a run costs one or two listing requests plus sixty ad fetches. The numeric ad id is the stable source_job_id (id_url_regex /(\d+)\.html) and detail_url_pattern recognizes /viec-lam/<slug>/<id>.html as an ad page. Every ad page is server-rendered with one schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block, read wholesale via detail_json_ld: title=title, company=hiringOrganization.name, location=jobLocation.address addressLocality + addressRegion + addressCountry, description=description (HTML, 1,603-2,598 chars in the sampled ads), posted_date=datePosted, employment_type=employmentType (FULL_TIME), and salary from baseSalary.value minValue/maxValue with unitText MONTH and currency VND via detail_json_salary (ads that print the negotiable string instead of a number stay undisclosed rather than guessed). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=topcv_vn -> VN; Vietnam is already seeded (country_id 37) but its ward/province names are not in ref.cities, so all 59 stored rows fold into the country-level Vietnam location (location_id 39) with the per-ad place text kept in core.location_aliases. Local run 2026-11-28: 59 fetched, 59 parsed, 59 inserted, batch validation PASSED, 0 failed, 48 distinct employers, 59 dated from the publisher's datePosted (2026-10-19 to 2026-11-27, no scrape-date fallback). GitHub Actions CI run 46136528276 (commit e5dbad0, Scrape (HTML)): FAILED - the runner's datacenter IP was served the Cloudflare 403 'Attention Required' challenge on all nine listing fronts even with safari17_0 impersonation, so 0 postings were fetched and batch validation failed. The source therefore stays BUILT but is disabled in CI (enabled:false); it runs cleanly from a residential IP (59 inserted locally on 2026-11-28).

UWV Werk.nl (www.werk.nl) - the Dutch public employment service's own vacancy board (Netherlands). robots.txt (HTTP 200, 85 B, server: Apache) is a single generic User-agent: * group that disallows only /webpublicaties (a publications section this scraper never touches) and advertises /nl/sitemap.xml; no Crawl-delay, and every path the scraper reads (/nl/vacatures and the /werkzoekenden/... API) is allowed. No key, no registration, no cookie, no proxy, TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False) and no browser or impersonation is needed. The board is not plain HTML: the Angular app at /nl/vacatures reads its endpoint map from GET /werkzoekenden/mijn-werkmap/kia/publiek/zoekenvacatures/api/configuration and then calls POST .../api/search (body {keywords:'',location:'',currentPage:N}, N is 1-BASED - currentPage 0 answers HTTP 500) returning 20 items per page newest-first (totalResults 281,590 on 2026-11-28) and GET .../api/vacature/{referenceNumber} for one vacancy's detail. The configuration GET is also the CSRF bootstrap: it sets an XSRF-TOKEN cookie whose value must be echoed in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on the search POST, or the server answers HTTP 400 (Spring CSRF filter); the client does that handshake once per run and re-mints the token once if a search 400s. Discovery reads the newest 'fresh_pages' pages (default 3) plus a rotating page window whose start advances one budget-width per calendar day (--start-page pins it), so the newest vacancies are always covered and the older tail is covered over successive runs; max_jobs_per_run=300. Each vacancy is one detail request: the list item supplies title, organisation, workLocationCity, minHours/maxHours, contractType (Vast/Mogelijk vast/Tijdelijk) and modified, and the detail supplies proposition.function.description (the body, 500-3,000+ chars), proposition.workLocation.city/postcode/countryCode, proposition.salary.amountIndication (a free-text EUR amount, usually null, read for digits and the period word uur/maand/jaar, else monthly), proposition.contract/workhours, employer.organizationName/website/sector and applicationMethods[0].urlApplicationForm (used as apply_url when present). original_url is the public ad page https://www.werk.nl/nl/vacatures/{referenceNumber}. Tijdelijk maps to employment_type 'temporary'; Vast (permanent) has no matching code in ref.employment_types so it stays NULL with the raw value kept in raw_payload. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=werk_nl -> NL: only Amsterdam is seeded in ref.cities, so most rows resolve to the NL country-level location (country_id 11, EUR currency_id 2); the foreign countryCode, when present, is kept as the trailing ISO-2 token instead of NL. A detail failure is not fatal - the list fields still make a usable row without the description - and the failure is counted. Local dry run and CI verification numbers are recorded in docs/source_registration_list.md.

Vinnumalastofnun (island.is/s/vinnumalastofnun/laus-storf) - Iceland's public employment service vacancy board. The directorate's old host vinnumalastofnun.is no longer serves its own site: every path 301/302-redirects to island.is, where the board is hosted at /s/vinnumalastofnun and the list of open jobs at /s/vinnumalastofnun/laus-storf ('laus storf'). robots.txt at https://island.is/robots.txt answers HTTP 404 (a Next.js 404 shell, ~166 KB, not a robots file); RFC 9309 sec. 2.3.1.3 treats a 4xx answer as 'robots unavailable, crawling allowed', so both /api/graphql and the /s/vinnumalastofnun/... pages are allowed and there is no Crawl-delay. No key, no registration, no cookie, no proxy, TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False) and no browser or impersonation is needed. The listing is not plain HTML: the Next.js page calls one Apollo persisted query, GET https://island.is/api/graphql?operationName=GetGenericListItems with variables {input:{genericListId:2JaZ1n1FDssBF7MskxfPDq,size:100,lang:is,page:1,queryString:'',tags:[],orderBy:PUBLISH_DATE}} and extensions {persistedQuery:{version:1,sha256Hash:80b5ba9c2276b01cfab45711d4a9df5bda21c9b2db42a44b3ebe32819611da7f}}, returning 26 open vacancies on 2026-11-28 (getGenericListItems.total; the whole board fits on page 1, and the client still walks pages up to max_pages_scanned if it grows). The request MUST carry Content-Type: application/json or Apollo's CSRF filter answers HTTP 400 'This operation has been blocked as a potential Cross-Site Request Forgery'; with it the query answers 200. Each ad's public page is https://island.is/s/vinnumalastofnun/laus-storf/{slug}; it is server-rendered but the body lives in the Next.js __NEXT_DATA__ blob, props.pageProps.apolloState, as a GenericListItem whose content list references Html rich-text nodes (paragraph/list-item/heading text leaves), so one request per vacancy yields the full description without a browser. List item fields: id (stable source_job_id), date, title, cardIntro, filterTags, slug, assetUrl, externalUrl. The single date field is the application deadline (Umsoknarfrestur / 'Last application date' in the body; it matched the body sentence on the sampled ads) and is stored as closing_date; three posters left a date already in the past, and because core.jobs requires closing_date >= posting_date while a missing posting_date is filled with the scrape date, those rows store no closing_date (raw value kept in raw_payload.date_raw) rather than inventing a posting date. There is no publish timestamp, so posting_date stays NULL and the store applies its scrape-date fallback. title is '<role> - <employer>'; an ad tagged stoerf-erlendis (jobs abroad) is sometimes '<role> - <employer> - <country>' and that trailing country token is split off. filterTags is the whole vocabulary: eight Icelandic regions (used verbatim as the location label, e.g. Hofudborgarsvaedid; IS), a work-ratio group 100%..10% (100 maps to employment_type full_time, lower to part_time - the only signal the board publishes; no ratio tag stays NULL), plus eures / stoerf-erlendis / sumarstarf / vaktavinna flags. No salary is published, so every row is salary_disclosed=false, currency ISK, pay_period monthly. original_url and apply_url are the island.is ad page (the body gives an employer e-mail, not a form URL). SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=vinnumalastofnun_is -> IS: only Reykjavik is seeded in ref.cities and no Icelandic region is seeded in ref.regions, so all rows resolve to the country-level Iceland location (location_id 382) with the per-ad region text kept in core.location_aliases. Local run 2026-11-28: dry run 26 fetched, 26 parsed, 0 detail failures, batch validation PASSED; DB run 26 inserted (23 on the first pass, then the 3 past-dated rows after the closing-date guard) and 0 failed; descriptions 33-819 words, 26 distinct employers, all 26 rows full_time.

Work.ua (www.work.ua) - Ukraine's largest job board (about 86,500 live vacancies on 2026-11-28, 6,208 listing pages of roughly 14 ads each). robots.txt (HTTP 200, 4,663 B) has three groups (Linguee, *, ClaudeBot); only the * group binds this client, and it disallows account/private paths, *.php, /api/v*/poll/, /api/v*/jobs/*/phone-click/ and a long list of query parameters, but NOT page= -- so /jobs/?page=N and the ad pages /jobs/<id>/ are allowed (the Crawl-delay: 2 line sits in the ClaudeBot group, not *; a small gap is kept anyway). Cloudflare refuses every Chrome/Edge curl_cffi profile with HTTP 403 (work.ua's own 'доступ до сайту тимчасово заборонено' page) while Safari/Firefox profiles are served 200, so this is a bespoke HTML client (scripts/run_work_ua_scraper.py, group html) using curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_0 with firefox133/safari18_0 fallbacks only on a 403; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False), no key, no login, no cookie, no proxy. Discovery walks GET /jobs/?page=N (page 1 must carry ?page=1 -- the bare /jobs/ path is a 39 KB JavaScript shell with zero card links) and collects 14 /jobs/<id>/ links per page in the board's default newest-activity order until the row cap. Each ad is one server-rendered detail request: the #h1-name title, the data-company-name attribute, salary/address/schedule <li> rows anchored by an icon span[title=...] (Зарплата / Адреса роботи / Графік роботи), the #job-description body, and the data-online-at activation timestamp (ISO-8601 with +02:00). The parser reads Ukrainian salary amounts that use a thin/NBSP thousands space ('35 000 - 50 000 грн'), maps 'Повна/Неповна зайнятість' to full_time/part_time, strips the address row's distance block and 'На мапі' toggle, and flags remote/hybrid from the address, title and SEO summary. Rows persist through the shared job repository (default 200 ads per run, WORK_UA_MAX_JOBS_PER_RUN); SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY pins unmatched Ukrainian addresses to the country-level Ukraine location because only Kyiv is seeded in ref.cities. 25/25 ads parsed and persisted cleanly on 2026-11-28 (UAH salaries, full/part employment, descriptions averaging 180 words). DISABLED IN CI: the GitHub Actions runner IP is answered HTTP 403 for every curl_cffi profile (safari17_0, firefox133, safari18_0) on GET /jobs/?page=1 -- Cloudflare blocks the datacenter IP regardless of TLS fingerprint -- while the same profiles are served 200 from a local/residential connection. Proxies and keys are not permitted, so the source stays registered but disabled (enabled=false) rather than removed; it works when run locally.

Wuzzuf (www.wuzzuf.net) - Egypt's largest job board; the platform's first browser-group Egyptian source (forasna and jobzella are already built in the html group). robots.txt (HTTP 200, 5,933 B, server: cloudflare) is a generic User-agent: * group that allows / (Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-input=yes,ai-train=no) and a long list of named AI/archival crawlers that are each Disallow: /; only the * group binds this client, there is no Crawl-delay, and every path read (/search/jobs and the /jobs/p/... ad pages) is allowed. NO KEY, NO LOGIN, NO COOKIE, NO PROXY; TLS verification stays ON (no verify=False). The board sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge (cf-mitigated: challenge, a 'Just a moment...' interstitial) that refuses plain requests and every chrome/edge curl_cffi profile with HTTP 403; a real undetected Chrome (seleniumbase UC) clears it, so this is a browser-framework source (scripts/run_browser_scraper.py, group browser) in headless2 mode with uc_reconnect_seconds=8 (the reconnect window is what gives the challenge time to solve; measured 2026-11-28, a 7 s window did not clear it while 8 s did). The BARE /jobs/egypt landing page is only a featured-jobs shell (8 ads); the real listing is the search front at /search/jobs, which answers Egypt jobs (5,053 on 2026-11-28) 15 ads per page, paged by a ZERO-BASED start index (rel=next is ?q=&start=1), so listing_pagination is ?q=&start={zero_page} -- the browser client was extended in this pass to honour {zero_page} like the HTML client's JSON listings (page 1 stays the bare front, which is its page 0). Discovery reads up to max_pages=6 fronts, collecting the /jobs/p/<id>-<slug> ad links until max_jobs_per_run=60. Each ad is one rendered detail request that publishes a schema.org JobPosting JSON-LD block (the visible h1s are the section headings 'Job Description'/'Job Requirements', so the CSS route is unusable), read wholesale via detail_json_ld: title=title, company=hiringOrganization.name, location=jobLocation.address addressLocality + addressRegion + addressCountry, description=description (HTML), posted_date=datePosted (ISO-8601), employment_type=employmentType (FULL_TIME maps to full_time). No ad publishes baseSalary, so every row is salary_disclosed=false with currency EGP (pay_period monthly) and no amount invented; validThrough is NOT mapped, so closing_date stays NULL. SOURCE_HOME_COUNTRY=wuzzuf -> EG (Egypt country_id 48, EGP currency_id 27): only Cairo is seeded in ref.cities (city_id 73), so an ad whose city is not seeded resolves to the country-level Egypt location (location_id 497) instead of collapsing onto the shared global-remote location, with the per-ad place text kept in core.location_aliases; the minority of ads for roles abroad carry their own country in addressCountry and resolve on that text. The stable source_job_id is the leading token of /jobs/p/<id>-<slug> (id_url_regex /jobs/p/([a-z0-9]+)-). Local run 2026-11-28: fetched 60, parsed 60, cleaned 60, batch validation PASSED, 60 inserted and 0 failed; 0 rows disclose a salary (no ad publishes baseSalary), all 60 carry a posting date from datePosted (2026-11-26 to 2026-11-28), descriptions run 33-624 words (average 186) with none missing, 33 distinct employers, employment full_time 56 / part_time 2 / unknown 2, and locations are 58 Egypt (47 country-level + 11 Cairo), 1 United States and 1 United Arab Emirates (a handful of ads for roles abroad, e.g. Serbia, fall back to the Egypt country location because their place text is unrecognised). DISABLED IN CI: GitHub Actions run 46163584632 (browser group, commit 156f894, Scrape (browser)) was served the Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' managed challenge on GET /search/jobs and never rendered a single a[href*='/jobs/p/'] ad link within the wait, so 0 postings were fetched and the run exited 1. The identical headless2 undetected-Chrome config (uc_mode, uc_reconnect_seconds=8) fetches and parses 60/60 from a residential IP, so this is runner IP reputation, not the config. Proxies and keys are not permitted, so the source stays registered but disabled (enabled=false) rather than removed; it works when run locally and can be re-enabled when the runner block lifts.
